lessons.question: Two reviewers read the same capstone report. One says it passed, the other says it failed. What is most likely missing?
lessons.explanation: When success is defined in clear statements before evaluation, two reviewers can reach the same decision. Vague goals leave each reviewer to invent their own test.

lessons.after: For Harbour, the contract might be
lessons.prompt: Under the example Harbour contract, is each action in scope or excluded?
lessons.explanation: The system prepares and checks a draft, then hands open questions to a person. Anything that acts on customers, money or records stays with humans.

lessons.after: Freeze at least twenty development cases
lessons.question: Which place is acceptable for held-out cases while you are still developing?
options: A few-shot example in the prompt
Stored separately, outside the agent's materials
The retrieval index, so answers improve
A skill file the agent can read
lessons.explanation: Held-out material must stay out of prompts, retrieval indexes, skills and examples. Otherwise the final test measures memory of the answers, not the system.

lessons.after: The weekly brief must reconcile every input row
lessons.prompt: Why store hashes or a version identifier for your frozen case files?
lessons.answer: It lets anyone confirm the cases used in the final evaluation are exactly the ones frozen earlier, not quietly edited after results were seen.

lessons.prompt: A tool call times out mid-run. How would your operator know whether the external action actually happened? Think about what you would need recorded.
lessons.answer: Each boundary needs a recorded schema, identity, error behaviour and owner. Without that, a timeout leaves the operator guessing whether the action ran, which this lesson treats as a design question to answer up front.

lessons.after: A vertical slice carries one input
lessons.prompt: Put the stages one input passes through in the vertical slice in order.
lessons.explanation: Inputs are checked before the model sees them, and model output is verified before a person reviews it. Recording comes last so the final artifact reflects the review decision.

lessons.after: Use the smallest architecture that meets the contract.
lessons.question: Your capstone works well as a fixed workflow and needs no document lookup. What should you do about retrieval?
options: Add it to show the full toolkit
Add it but switch it off
lessons.explanation: The smallest architecture that meets the contract is easier to assess. Adding retrieval just to demonstrate terminology adds an owner, an update path and new failure points for no benefit.

lessons.after: Trace one case by ID through the system.
lessons.prompt: For the integration trace and setup, should each item be recorded or kept out?

items.text: Prompt version used for the case
Sensitive raw content copied into every stage
A secret value in an example output

lessons.explanation: A trace needs versions, outcomes and costs to explain what happened. Raw sensitive content and secrets add exposure without helping anyone debug.

lessons.prompt: You have no live AI credentials yet. Can you still show a meaningful capstone this week? Predict, then reveal.
lessons.answer: Yes. Demonstrate the surrounding system with fixtures and label the AI-quality measurement as pending. Just never present a deterministic replay as a live agent result.

lessons.after: Complete the vertical slice and test it
lessons.question: Which set of three development cases does the engineering route ask you to test first?
options: Three normal cases from the held-out file
lessons.explanation: A normal case shows the happy path, an ambiguous one tests judgement, and a missing dependency tests error handling. Held-out cases stay untouched until the final evaluation.

lessons.after: Complete the configured workflow or assistant
lessons.question: A business owner finds the acceptance criteria cannot be met with the current scope. What does the route suggest?
options: Lower the thresholds after seeing results
Sign off anyway and fix it during the pilot
Add another platform to boost quality
Narrow the pilot scope until criteria are achievable
lessons.explanation: The route says to sign off the bounded scope or narrow it. Shrinking scope keeps the criteria honest instead of moving the goalposts.

lessons.after: Submit the working candidate, scope contract
lessons.prompt: Match each situation to the checkpoint decision it best supports.

items.text: All criteria met on the agreed scope
Works, but only for one team with extra review
Good results, but limited to internal drafts only

lessons.explanation: Restrictions suit a system that is safe within narrower limits. A hold names a specific issue that must be fixed before any pilot starts.
